response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), s AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(avg_net) OVER (PARTITION BY side) AS side_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net AS avg_net_fee_rate, cnt AS record_count, avg_net - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM s WHERE avg_net > side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Record count is the number of joined fee records in the group (COUNT(*)), including those whose rebrate is NULL, whereas the average net fee rate ignores rows where feerate or rebrate is NULL.
Groups whose average net fee rate is NULL (all rebrates missing) are kept in the side average calculation as NULLs, which AVG ignores, and are not listed.
If orders.recordvault is not unique, a fee could match several orders and be counted more than once; it is assumed to be unique, as the documentation says.

alternatives.interpretation: Record count counts only records with a non-null net fee rate (those actually used in the average).
